glosses: To destroy by fire.

examples.text: All four engines and the entire train were derailed, and owing to the fact that all the vehicles except the sleeping cars were gas-lit, the whole of the coaching stock except the two rear brakes was burned out, beginning with the two front coaches, which were completely wrecked.

glosses: To become extinguished due to lack of fuel.

examples.text: The candle finally burned out.

1847, Charlotte Brontë, Jane Eyre, Chapter XVIII
Mr. Mason, shivering as some one chanced to open the door, asked for more coal to be put on the fire, which had burnt out its flame, though its mass of cinder still shone hot and red. The footman who brought the coal, in going out, stopped near Mr. Eshton's chair, and said something to him in a low voice, of which I heard only the words, "old woman,"—"quite troublesome."

glosses: To become nonfunctional (especially of lightbulbs or similar light-producing devices).
To tire due to overwork; to overwork to one's limit.

examples.text: After six months of twelve-hour workdays, most people just burn out and quit.

glosses: To cause (someone) to tire due to overwork; to cause (someone) to overwork to one's limit.
To end one's shift at a job.

examples.text: I start my shift at three in the afternoon, and get to burn out at midnight.

glosses: To have one's tires skid against the ground; to peel off, peel out.

To make (someone) unavailable for work involving exposure to ionizing radiation by employing (the person) in such work until the person's accumulated exposure reaches the maximum permitted for an administrative period, typically a year.

examples.text: The repairs on this nuclear reactor have burned out every welder in the province.

glosses: To use up too much energy when first bowled and to therefore not finish strongly.
Nonstandard spelling of burnout.

examples.text: His burn out hadn't been caused by too many dead bodies; it was from spending his life doing for people what most of them had refused to do for themselves.

glosses: To cause (a structure) to burn to nothing.

examples.text: The police are hoping to find the people who burned down the cottage.

glosses: To burn completely, so that nothing remains.

examples.text: A fire which started in the bedroom caused the cottage to burn down.

examples.text: Lashed by mad rage, and scorched by brutal fires.

To move at high speed (so as to leave scorch marks on the ground, physically or figuratively).

examples.text: Men on cycles, lean-faced, unkempt, scorched along every country lane, shouting of unhoped deliverance, shouting to gaunt, staring figures of despair.

glosses: To burn; to destroy by, or as by, fire.

examples.text: Power was given unto him to scorch men with fire.
the fire that scorches me to death

To ride a bicycle furiously on a public highway.
To burn and hence seal open tissue using a heated article or caustic agent so as to stop bleeding or minimise the risk of infection.

glosses: Consumer, corroder ou endommager par le feu, ou par produits chimiques.

examples.text: Nulle main laborieuse ne relèvera les toitures enfoncées ; nulle flamme ne brûlera plus aux âtres désertés.

examples.text: Dans ce pays, on ne brûle que du charbon de terre, que de la tourbe.

glosses: Subir l’action trop vive ou trop prolongée du feu qui donne une couleur rousse ou noire et un goût désagréable aux mets.

examples.text: Vous avez laissé brûler ce rôti.

glosses: Échauffer excessivement, causer une violente chaleur, dessécher par une chaleur excessive.

examples.text: Le soleil lui a brûlé le teint.

examples.text: J’avais comme une barre à l’estomac, et dans le cerveau quelque chose qui me brûlait. Je fus près de défaillir.

glosses: Être dévoré d’une passion pressante.

examples.text: La dame brûlait du désir d’ébruiter une nouvelle dont elle venait d’avoir la primeur.

Les mains lui brûlent : Il est impatient d’agir.

glosses: Ignorer un obstacle ou une étape pour atteindre un objectif.

examples.text: Cette marche ressemblait à une fuite. Troppmann marchait devant nous […] Il se hâtait, évidemment, et nous autres nous nous hâtions à sa suite. […] Ainsi, nous brûlâmes le corridor, nous descendîmes un autre escalier.

examples.text: Mais c’est Scarbo qui me mord au cou, et qui, pour cautériser ma blessure sanglante, y plonge son doigt de fer rougi à la fournaise !

examples.text: Louis XIV et Turenne ont cautérisé cette ravissante contrée. Çà et là, des ruines attestent l’orgueil, ou peut-être la prévoyance du roi de Versailles qui fit abattre les admirables châteaux dont était jadis ornée cette partie de l’Allemagne.
